name: Clapham Common
highlights: One of London's most popular running spots, a large tree-lined common with open playing fields and many trails to tread.

name: Tooting Bec Common
highlights: Wandsworth's largest green space (92ha), a deceptively large perimeter trail mixing woodland, grass fields, a lake and a lido.

name: Wandsworth Common
highlights: A disjointed park split into ten sections with surprisingly good running loops beneath beautiful mature trees.

name: Streatham Common & Norwood Grove
highlights: A small hillside park with hidden surprises including The Rookery gardens and incredible views south from Norwood Grove.

name: Mitcham Common
highlights: A varied nature reserve emerging from its rubbish-tip and gravel-quarry past, with rolling man-made hills, woods, heath, ponds and a golf course.

name: Farthing Downs & Happy Valley
highlights: The southernmost point of any London borough, an enticing mix of Roman-history chalk grassland, abundant wildflowers and hilly trails.

name: Beddington Park
waypoints: St Mary the Virgin Church Beddington
highlights: A small park with two distinct flavours, grassy sports fields and landscaped formal parkland, split by the River Wandle.

name: Wimbledon Park
highlights: A small but inviting park just east of the famous tennis club, with a big grass sports field and a sheltered athletics track.

name: Wimbledon Common & Putney
highlights: Home to the world's oldest cross-country club, a huge 460ha maze of wood, grass and heath centred on the 1817 Wimbledon Windmill.

name: Home Park (Hampton Court)
highlights: Possibly London's most under-utilised running spot, with grassy plains, majestic tree avenues, roaming deer and a rare feeling of solitude beside Hampton Court Palace.

name: Richmond Park
highlights: The largest of London's Royal Parks (1000ha), a former royal hunting ground with roaming deer and arguably the best suburban running in the world.

name: Bushy Park
waypoints: Leg of Mutton Pond Bushy Park
highlights: Home of the founding parkrun and elite tempo sessions, a huge flat grassy swathe with deer, ponds and top-notch running surfaces.

name: Crane Park
highlights: A long, narrow park following the River Crane under an ever-present cover of trees, with the 25m Shot Tower to spot.

name: Hanworth Park
highlights: A former royal hunting ground and WWII airfield, now a pleasant open grassy plain with wonderfully soft trails.

name: Hounslow Heath
highlights: A back-to-nature scrappy heath of shrub, grass and wetland, a key London wildlife habitat with a horseshoe-marked bridle trail through the scrub.

name: Bedfont Lakes Country Park
highlights: A 73-hectare nature reserve with six lakes, well-kept trails and rolling hills for a family-friendly run.

name: Beverley Brook Walk
highlights: A way-marked trail sampling Wimbledon Common, Richmond Park, Barnes Common and the Thames Path, with the train home or a 16-mile double-back.

name: The Wandle Trail
highlights: A 14-mile way-marked trail tracing the 'hardest working river in England' through rejuvenated woodlands and riverside parks.

name: Julia Bleasdale's Loop
highlights: Elite runner Julia Bleasdale's marathon-training loop linking the parks of Richmond and Bushy with long, traffic-free stretches beside the Thames.

name: Two Palaces and a Canal
highlights: A scenic west London loop taking in the grand grounds of two palaces, Syon House and Osterley Park, finishing along a tree-lined canal towpath.
